newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher, aided by CBOT soy strength.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher, aided by CBOT soy strength.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher, boosted by local and commercial short covering sparked partly by the strength of CBOT soybeans, floor sources said.
Dealers also noted a slight improvement in crushing margins recently was mildly supportive. November canola closed $6.70 higher at $387.70 with other months $3.50 to $7.20 higher.
Flaxseed prices were also higher, boosted by gains in other oilseed markets with commercials featured buyers. November closed up $3.50 at $359.00.

Western barley futures closed mixed with the constructive impact of higher CBOT corn partly offset by the current slow pace of export sales. Nov ended up $1.50 at $134.60 and other months were off $1.00 to up $1.20.
Wheat futures ended higher boosted by commercial buying and the slow pace of hedge sales.
"Farmers are selling more barley than wheat," one dealer said.
Dec feed peas were steady at US$196.00 while oats remained tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
